description: Reviewed meanings and original examples for existing words. These overrides do not add words or change rarity. Dictionary adaptations and these contributions are CC BY-SA 4.0; see docs/dictionary-cleanup.md.

be.verb: To exist, or to have a particular state or identity.

do.verb: To perform an action or carry out a task.

go.verb: To move or travel from one place to another.

mean.verb: To signify something or intend to convey it.

steal.verb: To take something that belongs to someone else without permission.

ought.Definition: Used to express duty, advisability, or an expected result.
ought.Sentence: We ought to leave before it gets dark.
ought.reason: Keep the ordinary verb rather than an old variant of aught.

true.Definition: In accordance with fact or reality; correct.
true.Sentence: The story she told was true.
true.reason: Repair the spreadsheet-style TRUE spelling of an ordinary adjective.

okay.Definition: Acceptable or satisfactory; also safe or in good health.
okay.Sentence: Everyone was okay after the storm.
okay.reason: Retain an ordinary word whose source points to uppercase OK.

forth.Definition: Forward or outward from a place.
forth.Sentence: The children ran back and forth across the yard.
forth.reason: Keep a familiar word despite overly restrictive source usage labels.

gotta.Definition: An informal way of saying have to or have got to.
gotta.reason: Preserve an established informal spelling already accepted by the game.

means.Definition: A method of achieving something, or resources available for a purpose.
means.Sentence: The bicycle was her only means of transport.
means.reason: Explain the familiar noun directly; its root is missing from the source export.

abs.Definition: The abdominal muscles at the front of the body.
abs.reason: Keep the familiar muscle sense instead of the abbreviation for abstract.

bio.Definition: A short account of a person's life.
bio.Sentence: Her bio describes her work as an artist.
bio.reason: An established everyday shortening of biography.

app.Definition: A computer program, especially one designed for a phone or tablet.
app.Sentence: I use an app to check the weather.
app.reason: Use the familiar software meaning and a short example.

apple.Definition: A round fruit with red, green, or yellow skin and firm flesh.
apple.Sentence: She packed an apple in her lunch.
apple.reason: Keep the fruit meaning, remove the brand collision and archaic quotation.

orange.Definition: A round citrus fruit with a thick peel and juicy flesh; also the color between red and yellow.
orange.Sentence: He peeled an orange for a snack.
orange.reason: Lead with the familiar fruit meaning rather than the tree or Orange Order.

train.Definition: A connected series of railway cars; also the trailing part of a long dress.
train.Sentence: We took the train into the city.
train.reason: Restore the everyday railway meaning while preserving the valid dress meaning.

cat.Definition: A small domesticated feline often kept as a pet; also a member of the wider cat family.
cat.Sentence: The cat curled up on the sofa.
cat.reason: Replace a taxonomic heading and lengthy quotation with a clear familiar meaning.

dog.Definition: A domesticated animal related to the wolf, often kept as a pet or working animal.
dog.Sentence: The dog waited by the door.
dog.reason: Repair damaged characters in the existing entry, which is absent from the partial source export.

can.Definition: To be able to do something.
can.Sentence: I can swim across the pool.
can.reason: Use a clear explanation of the ability sense.

bank.Definition: A business that holds and lends money; also the land along the edge of a river or lake.

bank.reason: Provide familiar meanings and replace a long quotation.

bat.Definition: A flying mammal; also a piece of sporting equipment used to hit a ball.
bat.Sentence: A bat flew out of the cave at dusk.

crane.Definition: A large bird with long legs and a long neck; also a machine used to lift heavy objects.

rose.Definition: A flowering shrub with often fragrant blossoms; also one of its flowers.
rose.Sentence: A red rose bloomed beside the path.

run.Definition: To move quickly on foot, with both feet briefly off the ground during each stride.
run.Sentence: The children run across the field.

ran.Definition: Past tense of run: moved quickly on foot.
ran.Sentence: She ran to catch the bus.
ran.reason: Replace a grammatical placeholder example and explain the underlying meaning.

running.Definition: The present participle of run: moving quickly on foot.
running.Sentence: He is running around the track.

dogs.Definition: Plural of dog: domesticated animals often kept as pets or working animals.

rem.Definition: A unit used to measure the biological effect of ionizing radiation.
